description:
From the fz-kdt.127 cold review (2026-09-02, F4; pre-existing law,
observed under the (B) prototype on a_mixed). With the callable axis
PerPosition and recursing into captures, the covering seat reorders
a_mixed's arms wide-first (sound: output identical) and the grounded
specialization x23 becomes DEAD -- because `erasing_overlap` is
symmetric: an exact arm and an inexact (any-capture) arm are treated as
mutually erasing, so the exact arm can never be seated ahead even though
the hazard (routing a value into a body whose surface never named it)
only runs one way: wide-body-receives-narrow-value is safe, narrow-body-
receives-wide-value is not. A one-sided relation would keep exact
specializations live where the exact test is sufficient. fz-kdt.131
facet; characterize corpus-wide after fz-kdt.127 (B) lands (count exact
specializations made dead by symmetric erasing-overlap).

comments.text:
MEASURED at the fz-kdt.127.1 landing (f34c2aaa3). The one-sided-hazard
facet now has a live corpus instance and a name.

`a_mixed`'s callsite carries two arms over one lambda:
  wide  `closure[Enum.reduce/3#L](closure[Enum.each/2#L](any))`
  exact `closure[Enum.reduce/3#L](closure[Enum.each/2#L](closure[main/0#L]()))`
The wide arm's capture position is `any`, so `erasing_overlap` reports
the pair erasing, `covers` demands surface coverage, and the seat puts
the WIDE arm first. Sound -- its surface contains the narrow one, output
is byte-identical on all three doors, and the corpus behaviour sweep
moves nothing -- but the exact specialization x23 is still emitted and is
now unreachable. Executable count is unchanged at 28, so the cost is a
dead body, not a lost one.

This is the exact shape this ticket describes: `erasing_overlap` is
symmetric while the hazard (a value passing the NARROW test escaping the
narrow surface) is one-sided. A one-sided relation would seat the exact
arm first here and keep the specialization live. Reproducer:
`fixtures2/behavior/a_mixed.fz`, backend dump, the arm order at the
`Enum.reduce/3` callsite.

title: erasing_overlap is symmetric while the fz-kdt.131 hazard is one-sided: exact-vs-inexact arm pairs lose the exact specialization
